title: 2016 HMMT February Guts Problem 3

concepts.label: Triangle centers: centroid, incenter, circumcenter, orthocenter, Euler line, nine-point circle

statement: Let \(P R O B L E M Z\) be a regular octagon inscribed in a circle of unit radius. Diagonals \(M R, O Z\) meet at \(I\). Compute \(L I\).

solutions.text:
Answer: \(\sqrt{2}\)
If \(W\) is the center of the circle then \(I\) is the incenter of \(\triangle R W Z\). Moreover, \(P R I Z\) is a rhombus. It follows that \(P I\) is twice the inradius of a \(1-1-\sqrt{2}\) triangle, hence the answer of \(2-\sqrt{2}\). So \(L I=\sqrt{2}\).
Alternatively, one can show (note, really) that the triangle OIL is isosceles.
